authority: plans/LEVER_SWEEP_2026-10-06.md A4: 'Needs Arnav: no'. Tier A, so no number of record changes.
what: This is not a modelling round and is report-only. Each of the six records gets 90% group-conformal prediction intervals by group-weighted CV+ (Barber et al. 2021, Ann Stat 49:486). The weighting follows Dunn, Wasserman & Ramdas (JASA 2023, two-layer hierarchical conformal). Coverage is measured in a nested repeated GroupKFold 5x10 evaluation. Heat-flux Mondrian strata are used for the five FSRI targets. Group-level and row-level coverage are both reported, plus a report-only CQR variant (Romano et al. 2019, NeurIPS). The pHRR intervals are wired into demo/predict.py. No R2, CI, leaderboard row or number of record changes.
banned_moves_note: Checked experiments/banned_moves.md. No new feature, join or row exclusion: every record is re-fit on its own rows, features, groups and hyperparameters. No win-rule or R2-CI change: coverage CIs are new report-only statistics and never promote or demote anything. No 'beats SOTA' wording, and coverage is never set against any bar. Nothing is written to experiments/results/, because scripts/update_trackers.py would ingest it as an experiment. leaderboard.csv and the xlsx files are untouched. TTI keeps the 681-row record population; the 6 operator-flagged rows (B4 / D4) are not dropped, because that is Arnav's decision.

step1_reproduction: Before any conformal computation, and for each target separately, reproduce the record with eval_protocol.repeated_group_kfold(model, X, y, groups, log_target=<record>), where log_target is True for pHRR and FIGRA and False otherwise, then eval_protocol.bootstrap_ci(y, oof[0], groups). The mean and both CI bounds must lie within 0.002 of 'record'. If they do not, that target is BLOCKED: write a blocker per the exit protocol and continue with the others. This re-computes known numbers only. Keep the repeat-0 OOF for the per-row CSV and for the pHRR artifact check.

method.nominal: 90% two-sided (alpha = 0.10). This is fixed; there is no alpha flag anywhere.
method.score: R_i = |s_i - s_hat_{-k(i)}(x_i)| on the score scale above, where s_hat_{-k(i)} is the model of the fold that held out row i's group.
method.mondrian_strata: FSRI targets: stratum = nearest anchor in {25, 50, 75} kW/m2 to the row's heat flux, ties to the lower anchor. So 15 and 35 -> 25 and 100 -> 75. Calibration rows and the test row must share a stratum. LOI: one stratum. Per-stratum counts of rows and groups must be printed. The 15/35/100 rows are too few for their own strata, since a finite 90% bound needs at least 9 groups.
method.group_weights: Primary: within a stratum, w_i = 1 / (number of calibration rows of group g(i) in that stratum), so each material or paper carries total weight 1. W = sum of w_i = G_s, the number of calibration groups in the stratum.
method.cv_plus_bounds: Test x in stratum s; fold models mu_k, k = 1..5; calibration rows i in stratum s.
cv_plus_formulas: u_i = mu_{k(i)}(x) + R_i and l_i = mu_{k(i)}(x) - R_i.
upper(x) = the smallest u_i such that the summed weight of {j : u_j <= u_i} is >= tau.
lower(x) = the largest l_i such that the summed weight of {j : l_j >= l_i} is >= tau.
If W < tau, the bound is +inf / -inf; count and report these.
Use 1e-12 tolerance on the weight sums.
With all w_i = 1 this is exactly Barber et al.'s CV+: the ceil((1-alpha)(n+1))-th smallest u_i and the floor(alpha(n+1))-th smallest l_i.
method.interval_units: Bounds are computed on the score scale. Coverage = 1[lower <= s <= upper] on the score scale, which equals raw-scale coverage because the back-transform is monotone. Raw-unit bounds = back_transform(bound), then clipped to display_clip for display and raw widths only. Coverage always uses the unclipped bounds.
method.theory_note: CV+ guarantees at least 1 - 2*alpha (80%) under exchangeability, and is about 90% in practice. Exchangeability holds only between groups, so the group-weighted version is an approximation to Dunn et al.'s pooled-CDF estimator. The measured nested coverage is the evidence; the theory is not.

deployed_interval (what the demo and mod: One stated repeat: GroupKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=0) on all rows with the record's groups. These are exactly the record's repeat-0 folds. Use the 5 fold models plus each row's repeat-0 OOF residual, with group-weighted CV+ and Mondrian as above. It is built for pHRR only (demo).

nested_coverage_evaluation (the evidence.outer: For r in 0..9: GroupKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=r).split(X, y, groups). These are the eval_protocol / record splits.
nested_coverage_evaluation (the evidence.inner: For each outer fold, take the outer-train rows only. Run GroupKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=r) on their groups to get 5 inner models, fitted on clones of the record model on the fit scale. Each inner model predicts (a) its inner held-out rows, giving the inner OOF scores R_i, and (b) every outer-test row.
nested_coverage_evaluation (the evidence.interval: Each outer-test row gets the group-weighted Mondrian CV+ interval from the 5 inner models and the inner OOF scores of its stratum. The outer test groups are never in any inner fit or calibration set.
asserts: Outer train and test groups are disjoint.
Inner train and inner held-out groups are disjoint, and every inner row is an outer-train row.
Every row gets exactly one interval per repeat.
pHRR deployed artifact: its repeat-0 OOF equals the step-1 repeat-0 OOF (atol 1e-8 kW/m2).
nested_coverage_evaluation (the evidence.fits: 250 record-model fits per target (10 x 5 x 5), plus 500 HGB-quantile fits for CQR, plus 50 for step 1. Expected total under an hour: LOI and CR are the slow ones (blends with 500-tree forests).
nested_coverage_evaluation (the evidence.note: Inner models train on about 64% of the groups. The coverage measured is that of the procedure, slightly pessimistic relative to the deployed 80%-of-groups fold models.
nested_coverage_evaluation (the evidence.deviation_from_finding: The finding's sketch calibrates a held-out fold on the other folds' OOF residuals from the same repeat; those residuals come from models that trained on the held-out fold's groups, so the test groups would touch calibration. The nested design replaces it, declared before any result. It is stricter, not a choice made after looking.

metrics (fixed; headline order follows t.group_all_coverage: The finding's 'group coverage': the fraction of groups (materials or papers) whose rows are all inside their intervals. Per repeat, mean over groups of min over the group's rows of the coverage indicator.
metrics (fixed; headline order follows t.group_mean_coverage: Mean over groups of the within-group fraction of rows covered, with each group weighted equally. This is the estimand the primary per-row interval is calibrated for (a random row of a new material or paper). It is the one compared with the nominal 0.90.
metrics (fixed; headline order follows t.width: Mean and median of (upper - lower) on the score scale, unclipped; mean and median raw-unit width after display clipping. For log-scale targets, also the median of exp(score width), which is (1+hi)/(1+lo) for log1p and hi/lo for TTI. Widths (all forms) are averaged over bounded intervals only, with n_unbounded printed beside them; unbounded intervals still count in coverage (they cover on their open side). An interval with lower > upper (possible only for CQR) is empty: coverage 0, width 0, counted as n_empty and printed. Widths get no CI.
metrics (fixed; headline order follows t.aggregation: Each metric per repeat, then the mean over the 10 repeats (the headline) with min and max over repeats.
metrics (fixed; headline order follows t.uncertainty: Group-bootstrap 95% CI for the three coverage metrics: 2000 draws, a fresh np.random.default_rng(0) for each CI (each variant x metric x overall-or-stratum cell), rng.choice(unique_groups, G) as in eval_protocol.bootstrap_ci, percentiles 2.5 and 97.5. Per-stratum CIs resample only the groups that have rows in that stratum (G = their count). The statistic is computed on per-group values averaged over repeats: for group_mean, the group's mean over repeats of its within-group fraction; for group_all, the fraction of repeats in which all its rows were covered; row_coverage uses each row's repeat-mean indicator, with groups resampled. Also print the binomial reference SD sqrt(0.9*0.1/G): about 0.038 at G=61 and 0.029 at G=107, a 95% band of about +-6-7.5 points. The plan's '+-4%' is about one SD.
metrics (fixed; headline order follows t.breakdowns: All metrics are also reported per stratum (25/50/75 for FSRI), where group_all means all of the group's rows in that stratum. A diagnostic table gives row coverage and n per raw heat-flux value (15/25/35/50/75/100), without CIs.
metrics (fixed; headline order follows t.reading_rule (fixed, report-only): Applied to group_mean_coverage, for every variant, overall and per stratum: 'consistent with nominal' if its 95% CI contains 0.90; 'under-covers' if the CI upper bound is below 0.90; 'conservative' if the CI lower bound is above 0.90. For group_all, wherever groups have more than one row in the cell (overall for every target, since FSRI materials have rows at several fluxes; per stratum for TTI, CR, LOI and wherever 15/35/100 kW/m2 rows join an anchor), say it is expected to fall below 0.90, because the primary interval is per-row, not simultaneous; group_all gets no reading-rule label. No variant is ever called better or worse; the tables are only juxtaposed.

variants.P (primary, deployed): Group-weighted CV+, Mondrian by flux anchor (FSRI) or a single stratum (LOI), score as in 'records'.
variants.V2_row_weighted (report-only): P with all w_i = 1 (W = n_s rows), i.e. textbook row-exchangeable CV+. It shows what ignoring the grouping does. It reuses P's fits.
variants.V3_tti_pearson (report-only, TTI only): The Poisson-normalised score R_i = |y_i - mu_{k(i)}(x_i)| / sqrt(mu_{k(i)}(x_i)) in seconds, with u_i = mu_{k(i)}(x) + R_i*sqrt(mu_{k(i)}(x)) and l_i = mu_{k(i)}(x) - R_i*sqrt(mu_{k(i)}(x)). Group-weighted and Mondrian. Coverage and widths are in seconds. It reuses P's fits.

CQR (report-only).quantile_models: HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss='quantile', quantile=0.05 and 0.95 as two models, learning_rate=0.05, max_iter=300, max_leaf_nodes=15, min_samples_leaf=10, random_state=0). One spec for all six targets. Each is fitted on the score scale s with the record's feature matrix X (NaN-native).
CQR (report-only).score: E_i = max(qlo_{k(i)}(x_i) - s_i, s_i - qhi_{k(i)}(x_i)), using inner OOF quantile predictions.
CQR (report-only).bounds: u_i = qhi_{k(i)}(x) + E_i and l_i = qlo_{k(i)}(x) - E_i, with the same weighted CV+ rule, group weights and strata as P, inside the same nested outer/inner splits.

variants.never_used_for_selection: P is the deployed method whatever the results. No variant replaces P without a new committed config and Arnav's approval. No coverage or width enters any adoption rule, numbers_of_record.json, the leaderboard, or model choice for any target.

Print '90% prediction interval: [lo, hi] kW/m2', followed by the method, the stratum used, the number of calibration materials, and the measured nested coverage for that stratum and overall: group_mean with CI, group_all, row. If the full-data point lies outside the interval, also print one line saying so.
demo_wiring (pHRR only: demo/predict.py.path_in_data_material (--material presen: k* = repeat-0 fold of the material's merged group. Print 'Held-out prediction (repeat-0 fold model that never saw this material)' = expm1(mu_{k*}(x)). Then print a held-out 90% interval = expm1(mu_{k*}(x) +- q), clipped at 0. Here the calibration set is the rows in the query's stratum whose group != own group, with the usual group weights; G'_s is the number of those groups; q is the smallest R_i in that set such that the summed weight of {j in the set : R_j <= R_i} is >= 0.9 * (G'_s + 1) (1e-12 tolerance). If no R_i qualifies, print the held-out interval as unbounded. If a measured value exists at that flux, print whether it is inside the held-out interval. The existing in-sample point line and its caveat stay.

honesty_caveats (must appear in the repo: Exchangeability holds only between groups (materials or papers). Rows within a group are correlated, so the group-level numbers lead.
With 61-107 groups, a coverage estimate has a sampling SD of about 3-4 points (95% band about +-6-7.5).
The intervals are calibrated to the FSRI or RPUF-literature populations. They say nothing about new labs or other populations (MaCFP, cone-db).
Wide intervals are the honest form of known weaknesses: TTI at 25 kW/m2, and LOI paper offsets. They are not a defect of the method.
This is report-only. It never selects, promotes or changes any R2 or number of record.
TTI uses the 681-row record population. If D4 makes 675 rows canonical, re-run this config unchanged.
rerun_rule: Whenever a number of record changes (a B or C round, or LOI snapshot 4 under the snapshot rule), re-run this config's method unchanged on the new record before any interval claim is made for it. Method changes need a new config.
selection_rule: None. This is report-only and nothing is selected or adopted.
exit_triggers: None from coverage or width. If a step-1 reproduction fails, that target is FLAGged with a blocker and the others continue. A failed nested-disjointness assert stops the run with a blocker.
open_questions_for_arnav (do not block e: The demo serves only pHRR. Extending demo/predict.py to the other five targets (per-target feature lookup and CLI) is outside A4. Until then their intervals live only in the report and the summaries.

The plan says to lead with 'group coverage', which the finding defines as all rows of a group covered. This config leads with that number, but the deployed interval is per-prediction and is judged against 90% on group-mean coverage. If simultaneous coverage (all replicates of a new material) is the wanted guarantee, a group-max-score variant needs its own config.
